onion.servingNote: Keep onion to about 1 tablespoon or less if you are testing your tolerance.
onion.swap: Try green tops or chives instead.
onion.note: Onion is often high FODMAP in larger servings.

garlic.servingNote: Use a very small amount or skip it in the dish.
garlic.swap: Try garlic-infused oil or a pinch of chives.

apple.servingNote: A small serving may be better tolerated than a large one.
apple.swap: Choose a banana or berries instead.

milk.servingNote: Lactose-free milk or a small serving may feel easier.
milk.swap: Try lactose-free milk or almond milk.
milk.note: Dairy can be moderate depending on lactose tolerance.

wheat.servingNote: Portion size matters; smaller amounts are often easier.
wheat.note: Wheat can be moderate for some people.

avocado.servingNote: Keep portions modest, especially if you are very sensitive.
avocado.swap: Use a smaller amount or swap for cucumber.
avocado.note: Avocado can be moderate in larger portions.

oats.servingNote: A standard serving is usually a gentle option.
oats.note: Oats are commonly a low-FODMAP grain choice.

eggs.servingNote: A usual serving is often well tolerated.
eggs.note: Eggs are often a low-FODMAP protein choice.

spinach.servingNote: A standard serving is usually fine.
spinach.note: Spinach is often a low-FODMAP vegetable.

carrot.servingNote: A standard serving is usually fine.
carrot.note: Carrots are commonly well tolerated in moderate portions.
